chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Sa'd al-Iskaaf, who said: 'I do not know him except to say, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):'

'There was a worshipper among the Children of Israel to whom Dawood (peace be upon him) marveled. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Do not marvel at anything from his affairs, for he is a show-off."'

'So the man died, and they came to Dawood (peace be upon him) and said to him: "The man has died." So Dawood (peace be upon him) said: "Bury your companion." The Children of Israel objected and said: "How is it that you did not attend it?"'

'So when he was washed, fifty men arose and testified by Allah that they knew nothing from him except goodness. So when they prayed over him, fifty others arose and testified by Allah that they knew nothing from him except goodness. And when they buried him, fifty [more] arose and testified by Allah that they knew nothing from him except goodness.'

'So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawood (peace be upon him): "What prevented you from testifying for so-and-so?" Dawood (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, [it was] that which You informed me of, from his affairs."'

'He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "That is so, but a group of Rabbis and Monks have testified that they knew nothing from him except goodness, so I accepted their testimony over him and Forgave him for what was in My Knowledge regarding him."'

key_terms.مُرَاءٍ: Show-off (one who performs deeds for display)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the worshipper of the Children of Israel and Prophet Dawood's reaction to his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of 'Hilf' (oath/testimony) where the public righteousness of the 'Ulama' and Rabbaniyyun serves as a veil for hidden flaws, leading to divine forgiveness despite the individual's true state. It highlights the distinction between Allah's absolute knowledge of the heart and His acceptance of the community's witness, a principle often cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid to explain the intercession of the righteous. The narrative underscores that while Dawood (AS) knew the truth, Allah chose to honor the testimony of the learned, demonstrating the high status of scholarly consensus in spiritual matters.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim, Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Sa’ad Al Askaaf who said, 
‘I have no knowledge of it except that Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘There used to be a worshipper among the Children of Israel to whom Dawood<sup>as</sup> used to marvel (be amazed) at. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “Do not marvel at anything from his affairs, for he is a show-off”.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So the man died, so they came to Dawood<sup>as</sup> and said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘The man died’. So Dawood<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Bury your companion’. But, the Children of Israel refused and they said, ‘How come you<sup>as</sup> are not attending it (funeral)?’ 
He<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘So when he had been washed, fifty men arose and testified with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that they did not know from him except for goodness. So when they had Prayed over him, fifty other men arose, so they testified with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that they did not know from his except for the goodness. So when they had buried him, fifty testified with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that they did not know from him except for the goodness’.

So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Dawood<sup>as</sup>: “What prevented you<sup>as</sup> to testify for so and so?” So Dawood<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! That which You<sup>azwj</sup> Notified me<sup>as</sup> of, from his affairs’.

So Allah <sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “That is like that, but a group of Rabbis and Monks have testified that they do not know from him except for the goodness, so I<sup>azwj</sup> Allowed their testimonies over him, and Forgave for him (whatever was) in My<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge regarding him”.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, Alayhi al-Salam, issued a judgment. It was in the case of a virgin woman who was accused of fornication. He (the Imam) commanded certain women to examine her. They reported about her to be a virgin.
He (the Imam) issued a judgment that said, ‘I am not to penalize one on whom Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has placed a seal.
He (the Imam) accepted the testimony of women in such cases.”
